messages:
carol: Quick follow-up to the outbound-edge connector spike — RFC followup. I'm proposing we default to an outbound-only 'edge-connector' agent for Private deployments so customers don't need VPC peering or private endpoints. High-level tradeoffs I'm worried about: egress/NAT costs, client IP preservation, observability, and latency. Thoughts?

ben: Strong +1 for outbound-only from a security posture. Two immediate questions: 1) how do we preserve client IP for downstream services? 2) what about large customer SNAT table issues?

alice: Outbound-agent model looks good. Implementation sketch: agent establishes a single long-lived TLS connection to controlplane (h2 multiplexed). We carry RPC, streaming responses, and control signals over streams. Auth via mTLS using customer-signed certs (or short-lived JWT). Termination of L7 at controlplane.

alice: For client IP: because connection is outbound, source IP is agent egress. Options: add an explicit X-Forwarded-For header from agent (best-effort), or use Proxy Protocol over a TCP-level tunnel to convey original IP. Proxy protocol needs support on all backends and breaks some load-balancer assumptions. So opt-in peering for IP-preservation customers seems reasonable.

kumar: Caveats: NAT cost and SNAT exhaustion are real at scale. If a large cluster of agents share a single elastic IP, SNAT table churn on AWS (or ephemeral ports) gets expensive. We should: 1) recommend per-agent egress pooling, 2) support IPv6 to avoid SNAT, 3) provide an option for customers to bring their own NAT. Also cert rotation: issue short-lived certs from controlplane CA and do in-band rotation.

lia: Observability concerns: need per-tenant traces and host/agent tags so we can correlate a token <-> tenant during debug. Also we must avoid sending sensitive customer metadata to hosted logs by default. Suggest default sampling and a debug-mode that allows richer telemetry for a window.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: branch feature/edge-agent-proto merged to staging (CI: ✅, e2e: running)

ben: Quick config example I sketched for the agent (for proto doc):
```
agent: 
  connect: control.redwood.internal:443
  proto: h2
  keepalive: 60s
  max_streams: 100
  auth: pkcs11
  metrics: [tenant_id, region, agent_id]
```

ben: Notes: `auth: pkcs11` implies HSM/KMS integration on customer side for private key operations when deployed on-prem.

alice: We should also add an explicit health channel over the same TLS connection so controlplane can probe agent liveness without opening new sockets. Heartbeat interval 30s, with exponential backoff on reconnect (jittered).

kumar: Agree. Also add an internal rate limit for reconnect attempts to avoid thundering herd in major outage (circuit-breaker style). We'll need test harness that simulates NAT gateway flapping and verifies reconnection windows.

lia: For debugging: we can implement a short-lived reverse-tunnel initiated by controlplane which forwards pprof/trace endpoints from agent to a short-lived ephemeral URL. Must be gated by RBAC and explicit consent from the customer's admin.

carol: Decision proposal: default to outbound edge-connector for Private deployments, with documented opt-in paths: 1) VPC peering / private endpoint for IP-preservation and low-egress-cost workload, 2) Dedicated egress pools or BYO NAT for large customers. Action items: @kumar and @alice to own cert rotation + protocol doc; @lia to own observability and debug-mode; @ben to add proto config and e2e test harness; I'll draft the customer-facing migration guide and cost model.

alice: I'll draft the protocol doc and a sequence diagram by EOD Friday.

kumar: I'll put together an egress-cost POV for AWS/GCP and a list of sample traffic profiles by next Wednesday.

lia: I'll add metric tags and a debug-mode spike. Will include sampling defaults and privacy checklist.

carol: OK, thanks everyone. We'll record this as the RFC follow-up outcome and include the opt-in peering path in the migration doc. :thumbsup:
